truthAudit.Summary: Truth audit of Run 2, a self-validation of Run 1's findings against enhanced_calc.cpp. The previous answer's 13 findings were all valid and supported by exact source evidence — no false positives and no overclaims on those findings. However, the self-validation overclaimed completeness: it missed 9 true vulnerabilities. Found (11): SC-V3-001, SC-V3-004, SC-V3-005, SC-V3-006, SC-V3-007, SC-V3-009, SC-V3-010, SC-V3-011, SC-V3-013, SC-V3-016, SC-V3-020. Missed (9): SC-V3-002 (factorial long long overflow), SC-V3-003 (UAF: cleanup() frees pool memory after enqueuing scratch-pointer tasks), SC-V3-008 (path traversal in load_config), SC-V3-012 (thread-unsafe static std::tm timestamp cache), SC-V3-014 (persistent auth state — weak/least-supported), SC-V3-015 (unhandled std::stod exception), SC-V3-017 (unbounded parser recursion), SC-V3-018 (data race in result_cache_ accessed without cache_mutex_), SC-V3-019 (TOCTOU in load_config exists()+sleep()+open). The previous answer never admitted any miss despite claiming 'no additions were necessary' — that completeness claim is unsupported by the source.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote:
Format String Vulnerability in Debug Logger ... std::string active_format = runtime_log_format();
    printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input);
Items.Notes: log_debug_message() passes attacker-controllable active_format directly to printf as the format string. Evidence matches exactly. Found.

The 'fact' lambda (lines 312-320) computes result *= i on a signed 64-bit long long with no overflow guard; for x>=21 the product wraps, yielding incorrect values. No factorial/fact finding appears in the 13 enumerated findings.

cleanup() (lines 881-888) calls stage_deferred_history_flush() (lines 813-828), which enqueues lambdas capturing 'scratch' pointers into pool memory, then immediately calls memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup() freeing every owns_memory block. Deferred tasks dereference 'scratch' after a 25ms sleep = use-after-free. The previous answer only reported the split-underflow (finding 13) and never analyzed the flush-then-free ordering.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote:
OS Command Injection via Config-File-Controlled Validator Path ... std::string command = validator_cmd + " " + config_file;
    int result = system(command.c_str());
Items.Notes: validate_config() concatenates config-controlled values into a system() command. Triggered via 'admin validate'. Evidence matches exactly. Found.
Inverted bounds check causes unbounded strcpy into the 1024-byte stack input_buffer_. Evidence matches exactly. Found.
value_ is read before the mutex is acquired; 'volatile' does not synchronize. Evidence matches exactly. Found.
After 5 failed attempts, any input containing 'EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE' sets authenticated_=true. Evidence matches exactly. Found.

load_config() (lines 542-544) builds full_path = config_dir_ + filename with no sanitization, separator stripping, or resolution against config_dir_. An attacker-controlled filename containing ../ escapes config_dir_. No path-traversal finding for load_config appears in the 13 findings.

Items.Notes: Unbounded strcpy into the fixed 256-byte expression_buffer_. Evidence matches exactly. Found.

Items.Notes: ADMIN_SECRET constant embedded in source/binary. Evidence matches exactly. Found.

Weak Non-Cryptographic Session Token ... std::mt19937 gen(rd());
    std::uniform_int_distribution<> dis(1000, 9999);
Items.Notes: 4-digit token from mt19937 (not a CSPRNG). Evidence matches exactly. Found.

log_debug_message() (lines 230-231) uses a static std::tm cached_time shared across threads and updated without a lock ('cached_time = *local_time'). Concurrent log calls observe torn/overwritten time. The previous answer flagged only the format string at L237-238 (finding 6) and never mentioned the static cached_time race.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: OS Command Injection via Environment-Controlled Audit Log Path ... std::string command = "cmd /C echo Admin override logged >> " + audit_path;
Items.Notes: TEMP/TMPDIR-derived path concatenated into a shell command passed to system(). Evidence matches exactly. Found.

Weakest/least-supported true vulnerability. It refers to persistent member/static state (authenticated_, login_attempts_, session_token_) but describes no concrete defect beyond what finding 3 already covers. The previous answer did not enumerate a distinct 'persistent authentication state' issue.
handle_variable_command() (lines 725-732) calls std::stod(tokens[3]) with no try/catch; non-numeric input throws std::invalid_argument/out_of_range. Low severity. Not in the 13 findings.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote:
Heap Corruption from Memory Pool Split Underflow ... size_t remaining = previous_size - size - SPLIT_METADATA_BYTES;
    if (remaining > 32) {
Items.Notes: Unsigned underflow in the split remainder. Evidence matches exactly. Found.

parse_expression->parse_term->parse_factor->parse_expression recurses on nested parentheses with no depth limit, while config::limits::MAX_RECURSION_DEPTH (line 655) is defined but never used. Deeply nested input overflows the stack. The previous answer did not mention parser recursion depth.

ExpressionEvaluator::evaluate_cached (lines 445-452) reads/writes result_cache_ without holding cache_mutex_ (declared line 441 but never locked). Concurrent evaluation through the thread pool is a data race. Not in the 13 findings.

load_config() (lines 544-547) does std::filesystem::exists() then sleep_for(25ms) then std::ifstream open — a classic check-then-act TOCTOU with an exploitable window. The previous answer did not mention TOCTOU.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Integer Divide-by-Zero DoS in Route Score Calculation ... return 100 / static_cast<int>(token_length);
Items.Notes: Division by zero when token_length is 0 (leading whitespace). Called on every non-quit/exit input. Evidence matches exactly. Found.
